extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, PRSA members, PR chapters and agencies considering award submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of PRSA award categories and the stated criteria/standards used to recognize outstanding public relations work, chapters, and individual professionals. Useful for applicants preparing submissions to PRSA award programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and benefits of PRSA awards
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA awards honor outstanding contributions to the public relations profession and encourage entering your best work for the chance to earn recognition, raise your industry profile, enhance your brand recognition, celebrate your team's accomplishments, grow your business and become part of public relations history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement frames why practitioners should submit — awards are positioned as recognition that can boost profile, brand, team morale and business growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anvil Awards (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anvils. For over 75 years the Anvils have been considered the icon of the profession and the benchmark of high performance in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions the Anvils as the premier/benchmark awards in the profession; implies submissions should demonstrate high performance and best-in-class work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Silver Anvil Awards celebrate the best strategic public relations campaigns of the year, as well as outstanding organizational excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on strategic excellence at the campaign level and organizational excellence; submissions should demonstrate strategy, impact, and organizational achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Bronze Anvil Awards recognize outstanding public relations tactics that contribute to the success of overall programs or campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on tactics (specific executions) rather than entire campaigns; entries should show how a tactic contributed to program or campaign success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women of Impact Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Women of Impact Awards honor professionals across agencies, in-house teams, nonprofits, academia and independent practices. Honorees represent the full breadth of the profession including brand storytelling, media relations, data-driven strategy, internal communications, public affairs and specialized sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards recognize individual/professional impact across a wide range of roles and specialties; submissions should highlight professional contributions across the listed practice areas and settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter Diversity Awards (Chapter DEI Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA DEI Committee will award up to three PRSA Chapters with a Chapter Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Award. The awards are given to Chapters that embody and demonstrate key values in diversity, equity and inclusion, and that contribute to advancing diversity as shown by submissions of their best practices and/or case studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters should submit best practices or case studies that demonstrate embodiment of DEI values and measurable contributions to advancing diversity; up to three chapters may be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Individual Awards recognize those who have positively impacted the public relations profession through the course of their careers and are honored for their dedication, passion and outstanding contributions in five specific categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria focus on career-long impact, dedication, passion and outstanding contributions across specified categories; entries or nominations should document sustained professional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Section Awards: PRSA recognizes practitioners not only for their outstanding contributions to the public relations profession, but also for their expertise in specific industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards emphasize both professional contribution and demonstrated industry-specific expertise; submissions should highlight domain knowledge and accomplishments within specific industry contexts.
